answer: Continuous Activity Ledger. Each agent identity builds a public transaction history; its routing weight and payout share depend on sustained activity across a rolling horizon, so benefits accrue only to identities that persist and transact. A cloned identity starts at zero history and must replicate the full record — paying real transaction fees and latency for every prior event — before matching one mature identity. Below the oasis of established reputation, clones earn near nothing, and the river of fees drains faster than clones can fill it.
